title: Reconcile-loop sweeps hit 'database is locked' 8x/24h; the in-process signal-dual-write thread (Database.insert_signal) is inside a write in 8/8
note: MEASURED 2026-11-14T04:54Z to 2026-11-15T04:54Z (journalctl db_lock_diag, 8 events; 0 dual-write failures). Waiter: reconciliation-loop in order_monitor._sweep_package_close_reason_from_trade (6) / _sweep_stuck_linked_packages (2); contained, retried next pass, no money path. Thread tagged [db] at the moment of the lock: [signal-dual-write] at database.py:insert_signal in 8 of 8 (lines 1751/1808/1811 across deploys); once also MainThread journal_sync.py:journal_sync. Other processes with the journal open: none (4), web-api uvicorn (3; different pids across restarts), a 'python3 -c import sqlite3 ... backup' snapshot one-liner (1, 00:37:34Z). The desk-build subprocess (the DB-LOCK-HOLDERS-DESK-BUILD suspect) was never named. Database connection busy_timeout is 3000 ms (database.py:529). NEXT (holder fix, no new gate): measure how long the signal-dual-write insert holds its write transaction (commit per insert vs batched; WAL checkpoint on that connection?), then either shorten it (commit immediately, no long-lived txn) or give the reconcile sweeps a longer busy_timeout. Then re-read 24h with a target of 0 db_lock_diag from the sweeps.
